prompt.context_jp: フロント業務の合間に呼び止められた遠藤清美は、同僚の高橋孝介と向かい合って座っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: フロント業務の合間に呼び止められた遠藤清美___、同僚の高橋孝介と向かい合って座っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that frames Kiyomi as the already-known topic the narrator is tracking.

feedback.correct_en: Kiyomi has already been introduced as the chapter's viewpoint character; は marks her as the topic the narrator continues to follow.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make her sound like newly-introduced information (identifying who was sitting), but we already know her. を doesn't fit — she isn't the direct object of 座っていた.

contrast_examples.en: Kiyomi was sitting. (continuing with Kiyomi as topic)

contrast_examples.jp: そこに清美が座っていた。
contrast_examples.en: There, Kiyomi was sitting. (presenting her anew)

prompt.context_jp: 「あれができたのは… 俺が宇宙人だからなのよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: あれができたのは… 俺___宇宙人だからなのよ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that identifies Takahashi as the (surprising) answer to 'who/what could do that'.

feedback.correct_en: This is an identificational/exhaustive-listing use of が: 'the reason I could do that is BECAUSE I'M an alien.' It supplies the new, pinpointed answer.
feedback.incorrect_en: 俺は宇宙人だ would be a general self-introduction (topic), losing the 'because' punch of this answer-focus. に doesn't form the predicate here.

contrast_examples.en: I'm the one who's an alien. (identifying answer)
As for me, I'm an alien. (general statement)

prompt.context_jp: 高橋の言葉が空気の中に浮いたまま、しばらく落ちてこなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 高橋の言葉___空気の中に浮いたまま、しばらく落ちてこなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle used to introduce this new event into the narration.

feedback.correct_en: Narrative-descriptive clauses that present a fresh event or scene detail typically use が. His words 'hanging in the air' is new, observed information.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 高橋の言葉 into an established topic being commented on, which clashes with the sudden image. で doesn't work syntactically here.

contrast_examples.en: The words hung in the air. (describing a new event)
Those words were heavy. (commenting on a known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 頭の中で問いだけが弾んで、着地する場所を見つけられずにいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 頭の中で問いだけ___弾んで、着地する場所を見つけられずにいた。
prompt.prompt_en: With だけ narrowing it down to only questions, which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: だけが highlights 'nothing but questions' as the exhaustive subject bouncing around — classic が for exclusive focus.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would shift to 'at least the questions' (contrastive concession) and lose the exclusive 'only questions' feel. を doesn't fit the intransitive 弾む.

contrast_examples.en: Only questions remained. (exclusive focus)
At least the questions remained. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 清美の返事に、高橋は明らかに納得していない顔をしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 清美の返事に、高橋___明らかに納得していない顔をしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that keeps Takahashi as the current topic being described.

feedback.correct_en: Takahashi is already in the scene; は picks him up as the topic and comments on his expression.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce him as newly identified, as if answering 'who was unconvinced?' — the paragraph is instead describing him. に doesn't form the subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 高橋は納得していなかった。
contrast_examples.en: Takahashi wasn't convinced. (topic comment)

contrast_examples.jp: 高橋が納得していなかった。
contrast_examples.en: It was Takahashi who wasn't convinced. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 力の異常さは疑いようもない。しかしそれと、宇宙人という単語の間には、あまりにも大きな飛距離があった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 力の異常さ___疑いようもない。しかしそれと、宇宙人という単語の間には、あまりにも大きな飛距離があった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that sets up the 'X is undeniable, BUT …' contrast.

feedback.correct_en: This は is contrastive: 'the strength itself is undeniable — but the alien conclusion is another story.' It sets up the pivot with しかし.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just report a plain fact without the contrastive hinge the next sentence needs. も ('also') doesn't match the logic.

contrast_examples.jp: 力は本物だが、話は別だ。
contrast_examples.en: The power is real, but the story is another matter. (contrast は)

contrast_examples.jp: 力が本物だと分かった。
contrast_examples.en: It became clear the power was real. (plain report)

prompt.context_jp: 美波と葉月は、どちらとも取れない表情を浮かべたままだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 美波と葉月___、どちらとも取れない表情を浮かべたままだった。
prompt.prompt_en: The friends are already in the scene listening. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The two friends have already been established; は promotes them to topic and the sentence comments on their expressions.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present them as newly spotted on the scene, which doesn't match — they're the audience being described. に doesn't fit syntactically.

contrast_examples.en: The two were silent. (describing known people)
The two came in. (introducing them into the scene)

prompt.context_jp: 美波が財布から十円玉を一枚取り出し、テーブルの上に滑らせた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 美波___財布から十円玉を一枚取り出し、テーブルの上に滑らせた。
prompt.prompt_en: A specific new action by one of the group — which particle?

feedback.correct_en: In narration, when one specific person steps out of a group to do a new action, が picks her out as the fresh agent of the event.
feedback.incorrect_en: 美波は would frame it as 'as for Minami, …' — more of a general comment, odd for a one-off visible action here. も (also) has no antecedent.

contrast_examples.en: Minami stood up. (new action)
Minami is always quiet. (characterizing comment)

prompt.context_jp: 三人はしばらく黙ったまま、ぬるくなった飲み物に口をつけた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 三人___しばらく黙ったまま、ぬるくなった飲み物に口をつけた。
prompt.prompt_en: The three people are the established topic. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 三人 refers back to Kiyomi and friends we've been following; は keeps them as the topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like 'it was the three who …' as if contrasting with others — there's no such contrast here. で means 'by/at' and doesn't mark the subject.

contrast_examples.en: The three stayed silent.
Three people arrived. (presenting them anew)

prompt.context_jp: やがて高橋がゆっくりとこちらへ戻ってきた。
prompt.prompt_jp: やがて高橋___ゆっくりとこちらへ戻ってきた。
prompt.prompt_en: A fresh action enters the scene — pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: やがて…が signals a new event appearing in the narrative — Takahashi walking back is the fresh observation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 高橋は would turn the sentence into an ongoing comment on him, breaking the 'and then this happened' feel. に marks a target, not the subject.

contrast_examples.jp: やがて雨が降ってきた。
contrast_examples.en: Soon rain began to fall. (new event)
The rain was cold. (comment on known topic)

prompt.context_jp: フロントに残っているのは高橋だけだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: フロントに残っているの___高橋だけだった。
prompt.prompt_en: The cleft structure ‘The one remaining was only Takahashi.’ Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: In a 〜のは…だった cleft, は marks the presupposed topic ('the one who was still there'), and the predicate supplies the identifying answer.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜のが…だった is ungrammatical here — the nominalized clause before the copula takes は. を would need a transitive verb.

contrast_examples.en: The only one who stayed was him.
Only he stayed. (different structure, no cleft)

prompt.context_jp: 清美の頭の中で、ふっと一つの案が閃いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 清美の頭の中で、ふっと一つの案___閃いた。
prompt.prompt_en: A sudden flash of an idea — which particle introduces it?

feedback.correct_en: The idea is brand-new to the narrative at this moment — が introduces 一つの案 as freshly appearing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 案は閃いた would presuppose we already know which idea; wrong for a sudden flash. 閃く is intransitive, so を doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.en: A good idea came to mind. (new idea)
That idea is interesting. (known idea as topic)

prompt.context_jp: 高橋は明らかに緊張した面持ちで、ネクタイの結び目を何度も直していた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 高橋___明らかに緊張した面持ちで、ネクタイの結び目を何度も直していた。
prompt.prompt_en: Takahashi is the known figure being described. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: The scene has already set up Takahashi; は continues him as topic and describes what he was doing.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would answer 'who was nervous?' as new info — not what this descriptive beat needs. で marks means/location, not subject.

contrast_examples.en: Takahashi was nervous. (comment on topic)
It was Takahashi who was nervous. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: やがて着替えを済ませた由美が、深々とお辞儀をして退勤していった。
prompt.prompt_jp: やがて着替えを済ませた由美___、深々とお辞儀をして退勤していった。
prompt.prompt_en: A new character stepping into the beat — pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Yumi is being introduced into this moment of the narrative with a specific action; が presents her and her bow as the new event.
feedback.incorrect_en: 由美は would treat her as a long-established topic and sound like a general comment, odd when she just appears for this exit beat. に doesn't mark the subject.

contrast_examples.en: Yumi came in. (new on-scene event)
Yumi has already gone home. (comment on known person)

prompt.context_jp: 目線の動き、口角のわずかな引きつり、そういう細部を彼はいちいち拾ってくる。
prompt.prompt_jp: そういう細部___彼はいちいち拾ってくる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking what he is picking up on.

feedback.correct_en: 拾う ('pick up / catch on to') is transitive; 細部 is its direct object, so を is the natural choice.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would try to make 細部 the subject of 拾う, but he's doing the picking. に would mean 'into details', which doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.en: He catches the details.
The details bother me. (different verb, subject marking)

prompt.context_jp: 場所を変え、三人は少し離れた位置に集まっていた。高橋は反対側の壁際に立ち、耳を澄ませる構えを取っている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 距離___して数十メートル、普通なら会話の中身など聞き取れるはずもない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle expressing the manner/measure ‘in terms of distance’.

feedback.correct_en: The fixed expression 〜にして ('amounting to / in terms of X') takes に; 距離にして数十メートル means 'some tens of meters, distance-wise.'
feedback.incorrect_en: で would read like 'using distance' and doesn't form this idiom. を also fails to produce the set phrase.

contrast_examples.en: It's five minutes, time-wise.
The distance is long. (plain topic use)

prompt.context_jp: 「俺もね 若いころは 後先 考えずに ムチャやってさ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 俺もね 若いころ___ 後先 考えずに ムチャやってさ
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle marking ‘in my younger days’ with a contrastive-topic feel.

feedback.correct_en: 若いころは sets a time-frame topic with an implicit 'back then, (unlike now)' contrast — exactly his nostalgic tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 若いころが would make 'youth' itself the subject of 考えずに, which doesn't match. 若いころで is unnatural as a time-topic.

contrast_examples.jp: 若いころはよく遊んだ。
contrast_examples.en: When I was young I played a lot. (time-topic contrast)
I recall my youth. (direct object)

prompt.context_jp: 目線の動き、口角のわずかな引きつり、そういう細部を彼は___拾ってくる。
prompt.prompt_jp: そういう細部を彼は___拾ってくる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which adverb best captures that he picks up on EVERY little detail, one by one?

feedback.correct_en: いちいち = 'one by one / every single time,' often with a slightly annoyed nuance — fits Kiyomi's sense that he's catching every twitch.
feedback.incorrect_en: そろそろ = 'about time to,' and のびのび = 'freely/relaxed' — neither captures the exhaustive, nitpicky nuance here.

contrast_examples.en: He complains about every little thing.
Let's head home soon.

prompt.context_jp: 客足が途切れたのを___、高橋がバックヤードの奥から手招きしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 客足が途切れたのを___、高橋がバックヤードの奥から手招きしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb means ‘taking advantage of the lull, picking the right moment’?

feedback.correct_en: 見計らう = to judge the right timing / opportunity; it collocates with 〜のを to mean 'waiting for the right moment when …'
feedback.incorrect_en: 見逃す = 'miss / let slip' (opposite feel). 見下す = 'look down on,' totally wrong register.

contrast_examples.jp: 頃合いを見計らって声をかけた。
contrast_examples.en: I timed it right and spoke to them.
To miss a chance.

prompt.context_jp: 仕事と家事だけの毎日を思うと、それだけで___が塞がる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 仕事と家事だけの毎日を思うと、それだけで___が塞がる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which body-part noun completes this idiom for ‘feeling heavy-hearted’?

feedback.correct_en: 胸が塞がる is a set idiom meaning 'the chest feels clogged — heart feels heavy with sadness/dread.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 口が塞がる literally means 'the mouth closes,' used for shock (口がふさがらない for astonishment). 耳が塞がる isn't idiomatic for feelings.

contrast_examples.en: Just thinking about it makes my heart heavy.

contrast_examples.jp: 開いた口が塞がらない。
contrast_examples.en: My mouth hangs open in disbelief.

prompt.context_jp: 高橋の集中を無駄にしたくないという気持ちだけが___回りしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 気持ちだけが___回りしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which kanji makes the idiom ‘spinning fruitlessly / going nowhere’?

feedback.correct_en: 空回り (からまわり) = 'spinning in vain / efforts going nowhere.' It fits her anxious but unproductive state.
feedback.incorrect_en: 下回り / 後回り aren't established idioms for this meaning; they don't collocate with 気持ちが….

contrast_examples.jp: やる気ばかりが空回りする。
contrast_examples.en: Only my motivation spins in vain.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の努力は空回りだった。
contrast_examples.en: His effort was spinning its wheels.

prompt.context_jp: 高橋は困った顔で頭を掻いたが、断り切れない空気が場を___いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 断り切れない空気が場を___いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb best describes an atmosphere ‘enveloping / covering’ the room?

feedback.correct_en: 空気が場を包む = 'an atmosphere envelops the setting,' a standard collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 担ぐ = 'to carry on the shoulder' (physical). 刻む = 'to carve / chop.' Neither pairs with 空気 in this metaphorical sense.

contrast_examples.en: Tension enveloped the venue.
To engrave memories in one's heart.

prompt.context_jp: まるで手品師が最後のカードを___ように、指先だけをゆっくりと動かす。
prompt.prompt_jp: まるで手品師が最後のカードを___ように、指先だけをゆっくりと動かす。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb means ‘revealing / exposing’ the final card dramatically?

feedback.correct_en: 晒す = 'to expose/lay bare,' here used for a magician dramatically revealing the hidden card.
feedback.incorrect_en: 潰す = 'crush,' 探す = 'search for' — neither fits revealing a card to view.

contrast_examples.en: To reveal one's hand.
To look for the answer.

prompt.context_jp: 清美は腕組みをして、しばらく天井の照明を___んだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 清美は腕組みをして、しばらく天井の照明を___んだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb captures ‘glared at’ while deep in thought?

feedback.correct_en: 睨む = to glare/stare hard, often while thinking something over — exactly Kiyomi's pose here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 飲む = 'drink/swallow' makes no sense for 照明. 休む = 'rest,' wrong meaning and conjugation.

contrast_examples.en: Staring at the ceiling and thinking.
To drink water.

prompt.context_jp: 清美の中には、単純な怒りとは違う、___した感触が残った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 単純な怒りとは違う、___した感触が残った。
prompt.prompt_en: Which mimetic adverb matches a dull, heavy, gloomy feeling?

feedback.correct_en: どんより evokes a leaden, cloudy, gloomy sensation — matches 'heavier than simple anger.'
feedback.incorrect_en: きらきら = 'sparkling' (positive). さらさら = 'smooth / flowing' (light). Both clash with the heavy mood.

contrast_examples.en: I feel gloomy / leaden.
Sparkling eyes.

prompt.context_jp: Kiyomi switches to her front-desk voice to greet a guest.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as a hotel clerk's response?

choices.text: 承知しました 確認いたしますので 少々お待ちください
分かった 確認するから ちょっと待って
承知した 確認するので 少し待て

feedback.correct_en: This is the standard business-polite register for front-desk service — 承知しました + humble いたします + 少々お待ちください.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is casual speech, inappropriate for a guest. C mixes polite 承知 with a bare command 待て, which is rude.

contrast_examples.en: Please wait a moment. (polite)
Hold on. (casual)

prompt.context_jp: Takahashi insisting he's a real alien, not a metaphorical ‘monster’.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for Takahashi's casual, slightly rambling tone?

choices.text: 俺が言ってんのは そういう比喩とかじゃなくて ホントのやつ
私が申しておりますのは そのような比喩ではなく 真実です
我が述べる所は比喩に非ず 真なる存在である

feedback.correct_en: A matches Takahashi's actual speech: casual contractions (言ってんの), 〜じゃなくて, ホントのやつ. It fits a middle-aged guy chatting with a coworker.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is overly formal keigo, odd between coworkers mid-confession. C is archaic/literary and wildly out of place in a hotel backyard.

contrast_examples.jp: 言ってんのは、ホントのやつ。
contrast_examples.en: What I'm saying is the real deal. (casual)

contrast_examples.jp: 申し上げているのは、真実です。
contrast_examples.en: What I am saying is the truth. (formal)

prompt.context_jp: Kiyomi vouching for her childhood friends' discretion.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural in Kiyomi's reassuring voice?

choices.text: 今まで どんな秘密も 漏らしたことないから そこは 安心してもらいたいんですよね
今まで どんな秘密も 零したことがないから そこは 心配してもらいたいんですよね
今まで どんな秘密も 言ったことないから そこは 信じてもらわないと困るんですよね

feedback.correct_en: 秘密を漏らす is the fixed collocation for 'leak a secret,' and 安心してもらいたい fits Kiyomi's gentle plea for trust.
feedback.incorrect_en: B swaps in 心配してもらいたい ('I want you to worry'), the opposite of what she means. C uses blunt 言ったことない and a pushy 信じてもらわないと困る that doesn't match her softer tone.

contrast_examples.en: To leak a secret. (standard collocation)
Unusual phrasing; 漏らす is normal.

prompt.context_jp: Takahashi brushing off the physical cost of saving Kiyomi.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version is the most natural way to say ‘there's no substitute for a life’?

choices.text: 命には代えられないからさ
命には換金できないからさ
命には取り替えられないからさ

feedback.correct_en: 命に代えられない is the set phrase: 'nothing can be exchanged for a life / nothing is worth more than a life.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 換金 means 'convert to cash,' absurd here. 取り替える is for swapping objects and isn't used in this idiomatic sense.

contrast_examples.en: Irreplaceable by anything.
I'll protect it even at the cost of my life.

prompt.context_jp: Kiyomi explaining why Nakamoto's lie about being a single mom irritated her.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for ‘using X as a get-out-of-jail card’?

choices.text: シングルマザーを 免罪符に使おうとするの カチンと来てさ
シングルマザーを 証明書に使おうとするの カチンと来てさ
シングルマザーを 免罪符に使おうとするの ホロリと来てさ

feedback.correct_en: 免罪符に使う ('use as an indulgence/get-out-of-jail card') + カチンと来る ('to get annoyed') together nail the irritation at the manipulative excuse.
feedback.incorrect_en: B swaps 免罪符 for 証明書 ('certificate'), losing the 'excuse to avoid blame' meaning. C keeps 免罪符 but switches to ホロリと来る ('to be moved to tears'), the opposite reaction.

contrast_examples.jp: それを免罪符にするな。
contrast_examples.en: Don't use that as your excuse.

contrast_examples.jp: その話にホロリと来た。
contrast_examples.en: That story moved me to tears.
